body:
"Duplicate" action in the list properties dialog (Android: full; web: a
working button is enough, styling can be basic) creates a new list:

- Owned solely by the duplicating account. No other members or pending
  invites carry over, even if the source list has collaborators — the
  duplicate starts as a private, single-owner list.
- Name: "<original name> (Copy)".
- Copies list-level fields: category_order, and notes (once T-62 lands —
  if this ticket ships first, structure the copy logic generically over
  "all known list fields" rather than a hardcoded field list, so notes
  falls in automatically once T-62 adds it, with no follow-up code change
  needed here).
- Copies every non-deleted item as a fresh item (new id, new created_at)
  with all its fields: name, category, stores, quantity, price, note.
  Status is PRESERVED as-is (a checked item in the source stays checked in
  the copy, backlog stays backlog) — this is a snapshot/template
  duplicate, not a "reset for next week" action.
- Deleted (tombstoned) items are NOT copied.
- The new list's items get fresh field-clocks (ts=now, by=duplicating
  device) independent of the source's history — a clean new list, not a
  shared-history fork. last_touched_by (T-64, once it lands) on the new
  items should naturally be the duplicating account, since they're newly
  created field-writes by that account.

No new server endpoint needed: this is client-side orchestration (build
the new list+items payload locally from the already-loaded source list and
its items, then push as a normal sync batch) on both Android and web.

Platform scope: Android full support. Web basic support — the action and
its correctness matter more than polish there.
title: Duplicate list: copy entries + settings to a new solo-owned list
